description: Student's t quantile function F^-1(p; df) (location 0, scale 1)

tolerance.reason: p and df are exact doubles and 1 - p is exact for p >= 1/2, but in the tail the quantile is |x| = exp(L) with L = log|x| of the order of log(1/p) / df; rounding L (or 1/df, which multiplies it) to a double changes x by |L| times 2^-53. The largest |L| at a finite, normal quantile on this grid is 689.6 (df = 1, p = 1e-300, x = -3.2e299), so up to 7.7e-14 is unavoidable; 2e-13 allows 2.6x that and matches t_cdf. SciPy's worst error at the points it gets within tolerance is 1.3e-14; it fails 36 points: up to 4.3e-7 off at p = 1/2 +- 1e-10 for 1 <= df <= 20 (0 for df = 4), 5e-4 to 9e-4 off at p = 5e-324 for df >= 1000, +inf (wrong sign) at p = 5e-324 for 2.5 <= df <= 100 (also at 1e-300 for df <= 10), and quantiles capped near -1e153 for df <= 1.5

grid: df in {0.1, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 7.5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e8} x p in {0, 5e-324, 1e-300, 1e-100, 1e-50, 1e-20, 1e-10, 1e-5, 1e-3, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 1/2 - 1e-10, 1/2, 1/2 + 1e-10, 0.6, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999, and the doubles nearest 1 - 1e-5, 1 - 1e-10, 1 - 1e-15, 1}; p = 0 and 1 are tagged pole (the quantile is -inf and +inf); quantiles beyond the largest double (df <= 1 with tiny p) are tagged overflow
